summary: LLM inference costs scale linearly with token usage, and most production applications waste 50-90% of their spend on redundant context, oversized models, and uncached repeated requests. By combining prompt caching, model routing, and semantic caching, teams routinely cut API bills by 50-80% while also improving latency, since cached and smaller-model responses return faster. Optimization at inference time is the highest-leverage, lowest-risk lever available because it requires no retraining and often ships in days.

techniques.name: Prompt Caching
techniques.description: Reuse the provider-side cache for static portions of a prompt (system instructions, few-shot examples, document context) so repeated input tokens are billed at a steep discount or skipped on inference. Most major providers now expose this natively.
techniques.savings: up to 90% reduction on cached input tokens
techniques.example: Place your large, unchanging system prompt and RAG context at the start of the message and mark it with Anthropic's cache_control: {type: 'ephemeral'} so subsequent calls within the TTL reuse the cached prefix at ~10% of the input price.

techniques.name: Semantic Caching
techniques.description: Store past query/response pairs and serve a cached answer when a new query is semantically similar (via embedding similarity) rather than requiring an exact string match, eliminating the LLM call entirely on hits.
techniques.savings: 60-80% reduction on repeat/similar queries (68% hit rates reported)
techniques.example: Use GPTCache or a Redis semantic cache to embed incoming questions; if cosine similarity to a stored query exceeds 0.95, return the cached response and skip the API call.

techniques.name: Model Routing / Cascading
techniques.description: Route each request to the cheapest model capable of handling it, escalating to a larger model only when a smaller one's confidence or validation fails. Simple queries go to cheap/fast models; complex ones go to frontier models.
techniques.savings: 50-85% reduction in blended cost per request
techniques.example: Send classification and FAQ queries to GPT-4o-mini or Claude Haiku, and only cascade to GPT-4o or Claude Sonnet when the small model returns a low-confidence or 'I don't know' response.

techniques.name: Prompt Compression / Optimization
techniques.description: Trim verbose instructions, remove redundant few-shot examples, compress context, and use concise wording to reduce input tokens without degrading output quality. Tools like LLMLingua can compress prompts automatically.
techniques.example: Replace a 2,000-token instruction block containing six redundant examples with a tightly-worded 400-token prompt and two high-signal examples, or run context through Microsoft's LLMLingua before the call.

techniques.name: Output Token Capping & Structured Outputs
techniques.description: Set max_tokens and request concise or structured (JSON/enum) outputs so the model doesn't generate long, rambling responses. Output tokens are typically 2-4x more expensive than input tokens.
techniques.example: Set max_tokens=150 and instruct the model to 'respond with only a JSON object {category, score}' instead of allowing a multi-paragraph explanation.

techniques.name: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) Context Trimming
techniques.description: Instead of stuffing entire documents into the prompt, retrieve and inject only the top-k most relevant chunks, and re-rank to drop low-relevance passages, dramatically shrinking input context.
techniques.example: Retrieve 20 candidate chunks, re-rank with a cross-encoder, and pass only the top 3-5 chunks (under 1,500 tokens) to the LLM rather than the full 50-page document.

techniques.name: Request Batching
techniques.description: Combine multiple independent prompts into a single batched request or use provider Batch APIs, which offer large discounts for non-latency-sensitive workloads.
techniques.example: Submit overnight bulk classification jobs through OpenAI's Batch API to get 50% off standard pricing with a 24-hour completion window.

techniques.name: Streaming & Early Termination
techniques.description: Stream responses and stop generation as soon as the required content (e.g., a stop sequence or complete JSON object) is produced, avoiding payment for unnecessary trailing tokens.
techniques.example: Define a stop sequence of '}' when expecting a single JSON object so generation halts immediately after the object closes instead of continuing to narrate.

techniques.name: Fine-tuned Small Models for Narrow Tasks
techniques.description: For high-volume, narrow tasks, replace a large general model with a smaller fine-tuned or distilled model that matches quality at a fraction of the per-token cost and latency.
techniques.example: Fine-tune GPT-4o-mini or an open Llama model on 5,000 labeled examples of your specific extraction task, then serve it instead of GPT-4o for that endpoint.

tools.name: GPTCache
tools.description: Open-source semantic caching library that stores LLM responses and serves cached results for semantically similar queries using embeddings and a vector store.
tools.pricing_paid: Free and open source (self-hosted; you pay only for underlying infra)

tools.name: LiteLLM
tools.description: Unified proxy/SDK that gives one OpenAI-compatible API across 100+ providers with built-in caching, model routing, fallbacks, rate limiting, and cost tracking.
tools.pricing_paid: Open source free; LiteLLM Enterprise from ~$250/month for SSO, support, and advanced governance

tools.name: Helicone
tools.description: LLM observability and gateway platform providing request logging, cost analytics, caching, and prompt management via a one-line proxy integration.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier (10k requests/mo); paid plans from $20/month, with Pro and enterprise tiers scaling by volume

tools.name: Redis / Redis Semantic Cache
tools.description: In-memory data store with vector search used to build high-performance exact and semantic caches for LLM responses and embeddings.
tools.pricing_paid: Open source free; Redis Cloud free tier available, paid plans usage-based (pay-as-you-go and fixed tiers)

tools.name: LangChain
tools.description: LLM application framework with built-in caching (InMemory, Redis, SQLite, semantic), model routing, and RAG primitives to orchestrate and optimize calls.
tools.pricing_paid: Open source free; LangSmith observability from $39/user/month after a free tier

tools.name: LLMLingua
tools.description: Microsoft open-source prompt compression toolkit that uses a small model to compress prompts and context up to 20x with minimal quality loss.

tools.name: Portkey
tools.description: AI gateway offering semantic caching, load balancing, automatic model routing/fallbacks, guardrails, and cost/observability analytics across providers.
tools.pricing_paid: Free developer tier; paid plans from ~$49/month scaling with usage and enterprise features

tools.name: OpenRouter
tools.description: Single API aggregating hundreds of models across providers with automatic price/latency-based routing and fallback, enabling easy cost-based model selection.
tools.pricing_paid: No platform fee; pay provider pass-through pricing plus a small credit markup on usage

quick_wins: Enable native prompt caching (Anthropic cache_control, OpenAI/Gemini automatic caching) for your static system prompt and RAG context to cut repeated input costs by up to 90%.
Switch high-volume simple tasks (classification, extraction, FAQs) from a frontier model to a cheap small model like GPT-4o-mini or Claude Haiku.
Add an exact + semantic cache (GPTCache or Redis) in front of your LLM so identical and near-identical queries never hit the API.
Set max_tokens and request concise/structured outputs to stop paying for rambling, expensive output tokens.
Trim and compress prompts: remove redundant few-shot examples, tighten instructions, and cut RAG context to the top 3-5 relevant chunks.
